explanation: Christian Doppler described it in 1842. The same shift in light lets astronomers tell whether a star or galaxy is moving towards us or away from us.

claims.text: The Doppler effect makes the pitch of a moving sound source rise as it approaches and fall as it moves away.
The Coriolis, greenhouse and butterfly effects have nothing to do with the changing pitch of a passing siren.
Christian Doppler described the effect in 1842.
Astronomers use the Doppler shift of light to tell whether stars and galaxies are moving towards or away from Earth.

evidence.restatement: The Doppler effect raises the heard pitch of an approaching source and lowers it as the source moves away.
The Coriolis effect concerns rotating frames, the greenhouse effect atmospheric warming and the butterfly effect chaos; none changes a siren's pitch.
Christian Doppler presented his paper on the effect in Prague in 1842.
